subject.title: Inconsistent message:sent / message_sent hook coverage across multiple outbound dispatch paths

question: Should the remaining outbound lifecycle hook coverage be centralized behind one shared exactly-once delivery observer/reporting seam, or split into per-surface fixes for Gateway/WebChat/TUI/native channel delivery?
rationale: The remaining gaps cross core Gateway/TUI surfaces, plugin-owned self-delivery, public hook semantics, and security-sensitive rewrite/audit behavior, so automation should not choose the permanent hook boundary by itself.

options.title: Centralize Delivery Observer
options.body: Create a shared reporting/observer seam used by core, Gateway/TUI, and plugin-handled delivery so hook emission is consistent and exactly-once across surfaces.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Surface Fixes
options.body: Keep this umbrella open while landing separate fixes for Gateway chat, TUI, OpenAI-compatible HTTP, and native plugin self-delivery paths with explicit parity tests.

options.title: Document Intentional Non-Coverage
options.body: Close the umbrella only if maintainers explicitly decide some delivery surfaces should not emit outbound lifecycle hooks and document that contract.

recommendation.title: Centralize Delivery Observer
recommendation.body: Create a shared reporting/observer seam used by core, Gateway/TUI, and plugin-handled delivery so hook emission is consistent and exactly-once across surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining decision spans Gateway/TUI lifecycle and outbound architecture, where recent adjacent history makes this the best available routing owner.
